name: Thirty-One (Scat)
description: Thirty-One, also known as Scat or Blitz, is a classic accumulation game for two or more players. The goal is to obtain a hand with a point total as close to 31 as possible in a single suit. It is widely played in Northwest Europe and North America and is a staple of pub culture.

overview.description: Thirty-One, also known as Scat or Blitz, is a classic accumulation game for two or more players. The goal is to obtain a hand with a point total as close to 31 as possible in a single suit. It is widely played in Northwest Europe and North America and is a staple of pub culture.

history.origins: The game's roots go back to the 15th century, with variants like 'Vingt-et-un' and 'Bone-Ace'. The modern form solidified in the 19th century.
timeline: 15th Century: Early '31' games documented in France and England.
19th Century: Becomes a popular gambling and social game in Europe.
Modern Era: Widely known as Blitz or Scat in various regions.
history.cultural: Often played as a low-stakes gambling game with three lives represented by coins.
history.evolution: Connected to the commerce and fishing game families, prioritizing card values within a single suit.

setup.players: From 2 to 9 or more people can play. The game is often best with 3 players but works well with a larger group.
setup.dealing: Dealer deals 3 cards to each player, one at a time, and 3 cards face-up to the table (the 'widow'). Remaining cards form the stock.
setup.equipment: Standard deck, three coins or tokens per player (for lives), score sheet.

rules.objective: Have a hand with a total value closer to 31 than your opponents in a single suit.
rules.gameplay:
1. On your turn, you may:
   a) Exchange one card from your hand with one card from the widow.
   b) Exchange your entire hand for all three cards in the widow.
   c) Knock, if you believe your hand is high enough to win.
2. When a player knocks, every other player gets one final turn.
3. SCORING: Total up cards of the same suit. Ace=11, K/Q/J=10, 2-10=face value. Three of a kind (any suit) = 30.5 points.
4. LIVES: The player with the lowest score loses one life. At zero lives, they are 'on the bus' and out if they lose again.
keyRules: Only cards of the same suit can be summed (except for three of a kind).
Three of a kind is always exactly 30.5 points.
A hand of 31 is an immediate 'Blitz', stopping the game instantly.
If you knock and tie for the lowest score, you do not lose a life, but others do.

strategy.basic: Collect high cards of a single suit. Don't hold onto low cards even if they are Aces in a different suit.
strategy.intermediate: Watch the widow cards that opponents take; track which suits are being 'drained' from the shared pool.
strategy.advanced: Tactical knocking: If you have 25+ points early, knocking might catch opponents before they can assemble a viable hand.
tips: Aim for Aces and Face cards of the same suit.
If you see a player taking many cards of one suit, avoid that suit if possible.
Knocking early can be a powerful bluff.

variations.name: Blitz
variations.description: Standard North American name where 31 is called a Blitz.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Blitz is a naming variant only; rules and engine match the base game.

scoring.description: Total same-suit cards. Highest hand wins. Lowest hand loses a life (coin).

synthesis.shortDescription: A fast-paced card game where you swap cards with a central 'widow' to build a hand total of 31 in a single suit. Knock when you're ready to challenge the table.

hero.title: THIRTY-ONE
hero.subtitle: The Blitz Game
hero.tagline: Suit up to 31. Outwit the market. Don't be the last on the bus.
